existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: CareTeam has material local breaking changes from R4 to R6. The top migration concerns are removed/renamed CareTeam elements, the `participant.role` repeatability narrowing, and R6 participant/reason content that R4 cannot fully represent. Confidence is high for structural deltas and medium for terminology impact because full expansions were not performed.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly a structural transform rather than a simple version-label update. R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` should be converted into R6 `reason` CodeableReference entries; R4 `participant.period` should become `participant.effectivePeriod`; participants with multiple roles should be split; and old `encounter` links need a policy, potentially updating R6 `Encounter.careTeam`. R6-to-R4 conversion needs loss rules for `effectiveTiming`, `supportingInfo`, broader participant references, and CodeableReference entries that carry both concept and reference.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, reference target, constraint, and required status-code conclusions because they come directly from the local StructureDefinitions and CodeSystem/ValueSet files. Confidence is medium for example-bound terminology impact because SNOMED CT and LOINC expansions were not available, and medium for change justification because official diff narrative or issue history was not supplied.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
CareTeam keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 4 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 3 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 52/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

3 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: CareTeam.encounter was removed from the CareTeam resource
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 CareTeam instances with `encounter` contain an unknown element in R6; preserving the relationship may require updating a separate Encounter resource.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: CareTeam.reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into CareTeam.reason CodeableReference
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: the R4 wire names disappear and SDK/FHIRPath paths change; reverse conversion can lose the explicit pairing when an R6 CodeableReference has both concept and reference.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: CareTeam.participant.period was replaced by participant.effective[x]
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid, runtime/API/codegen, and R6-to-R4 loss: R4 `period` is not an R6 element, R6 uses `effectivePeriod`/`effectiveTiming`, and `effectiveTiming` has no native R4 CareTeam slot.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: CareTeam.participant.role maximum cardinality decreased from many to one
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: an R4 participant with two or more roles violates the R6 max cardinality and code must handle repeated participant rows instead of a role list.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Participant member and onBehalfOf reference domains were widened and onBehalfOf semantics changed
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen only: new broad R6 references may not fit strict R4 models and old code may need type guards, but R4-valid references remain structurally valid in R6.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: CareTeam.participant.supportingInfo was added with no R4 equivalent
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new R6 supporting references have no native R4 CareTeam field; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
